drafts.walkScript: Start with the ones: 8 times 6 is 48. Write 8 and carry 4 into the tens. Then 4 times 6 is 24, and 24 plus the carried 4 is 28. So 48 x 6 is 288. Adding the carried 4 twice gives 328, not 288.

Start with the ones: 2 take away 5 will not go. Exchange across the zeros, so 4,002 becomes 3 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 12 ones. Now 12 take 5 is 7, and 9 take 7 is 2. Then 9 take 3 is 6, and 3 take 1 is 2, giving 2627. Rounding to 4,000 take 1,400 gives 2600, which is only close.

Start with the dark ones: one eighth of 32 is 4, so 3/8 is 12. Take 12 from 32 to leave 20 chocolates. One quarter of 20 is 5, so 5 are white. A quarter of all 32 gives 8, but the quarter is only of the 20 left.

Start with Monday: one fifth of 40 is 8, so 3/5 is 24. That leaves 40 take 24, which is 16 litres. On Tuesday a quarter of 16 is 4, so 12 litres are left. A quarter of all 40 leaves 6, but Tuesday takes a quarter of what is left.

Change means taking £2.80 away from £7.00. Count on from £2.80: 20p makes £3.00. Then £4 more makes £7.00. So the change is £4 and 20p, which is £4.20. Adding the two amounts gives £9.80, but change means taking away.

Change means taking £6.05 away from the £10 note. Count on from £6.05: 95p makes £7.00. Then £3 more makes £10.00. So the change is £3 and 95p, which is £3.95. Adding the two amounts gives £16.05, but change means taking away.

Start by adding the two prices: £2.45 and £1.30 make £3.75. Then take £3.75 away from the £5 note. Count on from £3.75: 25p makes £4.00, and £1 more makes £5.00. So the change is £1.25. Adding the note as well gives £8.75, but change means taking away.
Add the ones first: 5 plus 8 is 13, so write 3 and carry 1. Tens: 6 plus 1 plus the carried 1 is 8. Hundreds: 4 plus 2 is 6. So 465 + 218 is 683. Forgetting the carried 1 gives 673.
Start with the ones: 7 times 4 is 28. Write 8 and carry 2 into the tens. Then 5 times 4 is 20, and 20 plus the carried 2 is 22. So 57 x 4 is 228. Adding the carried 2 twice gives 248, not 228.

25% is the same as one quarter. One quarter of £64 is £16, so the discount is £16. Take £16 from £64 to leave £48. Stopping at £16 finds the discount, not the sale price. Taking £25 off gives £39, but 25% is a share, not £25.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. So the other angle is 180° take away 137°. 180 take 130 is 50, and 50 take 7 is 43. The other angle is 43°. Using 360° for a full turn instead gives 223°.

Start on the straight line, where angles add up to 180°. The triangle's angle next to 140° is 180° take 140°, which is 40°. A triangle's angles also add up to 180°. Take away 40° and 30° to leave 110°. Stopping at 40° finds the first angle, not the third.

Add the ones first: 5 plus 6 is 11, so write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 7 plus 4 plus 1 is 12, so write 2 and carry 1. Hundreds: 3 plus 2 plus 1 is 6, so the total is 621 g. Forgetting the last carried 1 gives 521 g.
